newsitem.title: UK: Clarke favourite to become UK Conservative leader.
newsitem.headline: Clarke favourite to become UK Conservative leader.

text.p: Former chancellor minister Kenneth Clarke is still favourite to become the next leader of the British Conservative Party at odds of 10-11, bookmakers Coral said on Monday.

Former Welsh Secretary William Hague is second favourite at 5-2, followed by by former home secretary Michael Howard at 4-1, former social security secretary Peter Lilley at 5-1 and arch "Eurosceptic" John Redwood at 33-1.

The 164 Conservative members of parliament left in the House of Commons after their May 1 election trouncing at the hands of Labour vote in the first round of their party leadership contest on Tuesday.
Coral said the betting was becoming much closer.
"In the last 24 hours we have taken hundreds of pounds of bets on Michael Howard and Peter Lilley, and the odds have shortened considerably," said Coral spokesman Simon Clare.
"Of the five candidates, only John Redwood has not been well supported, which could well be reflected in the number of votes he gets tomorrow," Clare added. --London Newsroom +44-171-542-7947
